lines.text: Your security lead asks a simple question. What did the agent actually run last Tuesday?
Without a record, you start digging. Terminal scrollback is gone, and nobody remembers which command ran.
Agent R Q keeps a searchable trajectory of every tool call and message in each task run.
Open the task from last Tuesday, and switch to the Trajectory tab. The whole run is there.
Entries are grouped into lanes, in order, so you can follow the run from the first message to the last.
Search for the command you care about, like curl, and the matching entries rise to the top.
Each entry shows what ran, and whether it was allowed or denied.
Click an entry for the exact input, the decision, the person who made it, and the time.
Approvals are part of the record too, so you can show that a person said no to the risky command.
So the answer to your security lead takes seconds. Nothing to guess, nothing to dig up.
The record is always on, so every run is audit ready, whether or not anyone asked in advance.
What would your security team want to see in an agent log? Tell us below, and try it at Agent R Q dot com.
